title: The dropped socket that nearly set off America's biggest warhead
hook: A dropped tool punctured a nuclear missile in an Arkansas silo.
summary: In 1980 a repairman dropped a socket in an Arkansas Titan II silo; it punctured the fuel tank, the missile exploded, and its warhead landed nearby without detonating.
sources: Wikipedia: 1980 Damascus Titan missile explosion: 18 September 1980, socket dropped about 70 feet, punctured first-stage fuel tank, explosion next morning, W53 nine-megaton warhead found in a ditch, did not detonate, one airman killed.
Eric Schlosser, Command and Control (2013) and US Air Force accident records on the Titan II Damascus incident.

lines.text: A dropped tool nearly set off America's biggest nuclear warhead.
lines.caps: A dropped *tool | *nearly set off | America's biggest *warhead

lines.text: In September nineteen eighty, a repairman in an Arkansas missile silo dropped a heavy socket.
It fell seventy feet and punctured the rocket's fuel tank.
lines.caps: It fell *seventy feet | and *punctured | the *fuel tank

lines.text: Fuel leaked for hours, and everyone nearby was evacuated.
Then the missile exploded, and the warhead flew across the ground.
It landed in a ditch, and it never went off.
lines.caps: It landed in a *ditch, | and *never | went *off

lines.text: One airman died, but a nine megaton blast was avoided.
All because one small tool slipped.

post.caption:
A single socket fell seventy feet and nearly changed Arkansas forever.
Would you have guessed such a small thing could cause this?
Follow @unt.oldfiles for a new untold story every day.
